summary_paragraph: A 46-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for severe abdominal pain and hypertensive urgency. She presented with intractable pain, elevated blood pressure up to 260 mmHg systolic, hyperglycemia, and signs of volume depletion. Initial management included IV fluids, insulin, and pain control. Due to worsening hypertension, she was transferred to the MICU where labetalol helped stabilize her blood pressure. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal pathology, and her symptoms were attributed to a functional gastrointestinal disorder rather than confirmed gastroparesis. Her renal function and hyponatremia improved with hydration. Leukocytosis and thrombocytosis were noted but deemed chronic. She was discharged home with improved pain control, stable vital signs, and instructions to follow up with gastroenterology and primary care for ongoing evaluation.
